detail.longDescription: From Zero Trust to Agent Trust: Securing AI Agents at Scale As organizations deploy autonomous AI agents across enterprise infrastructure, traditional zero trust security is no longer enough. AI agents can operate at machine speed, execute thousands of actions, and create serious security risks even when each individual action is authorized. Teleport’s white paper introduces three principles for extending zero trust to the agentic AI era: • Enforce continuously: Give every AI agent a unique, verifiable identity, short-lived permissions, and an isolated runtime that limits access and contains potential damage. • Bound collective autonomy: Establish guardrails for groups of agents so individually authorized actions cannot combine into destructive outcomes. High-impact decisions should trigger additional review or approval. • Assume misalignment: Continuously monitor agent behavior for deviations from intended objectives, including prompt injection, memory poisoning, and other forms of manipulation. Key takeaway: Securing AI agents requires more than identity verification and least-privilege access. Organizations must also control collective behavior, monitor for misalignment, and enforce boundaries at runtime. The path forward starts with a strong zero trust foundation, unified identity governance, just-in-time access, and auditable agent activity. These capabilities will be essential as autonomous AI becomes more deeply integrated into production environments. # Cybersecurity # ZeroTrust # AgenticAI # AISecurity # IdentitySecurity # CloudSecurity # AI # DevSecOps https:// goteleport.com/resources/white -papers/zero-trust-to-agent-trust/
